50th Reunion of Harvard Law School Class of 1948

The Need for More Multidisciplinary Skills from Professionals: Educational Implications专业人士为何需要更多跨学科能力

Today I am going to engage in a game reminding us of our old professors: Socratic solitaire. I will ask and briefly answer five questions:

今天，我想玩一个让我们想起昔日恩师的小游戏：苏格拉底式自问自答。我将提出五个问题，并逐一简要作答。

01Do broadscale professionals need more multidisciplinary skill?
02Was our education sufficiently multidisciplinary?
03In elite, broadscale soft science, what is the essential nature of practicable, best-form multidisciplinary education?
04In the last 50 years, how far has elite academia progressed toward attainable best-form multidisciplinarity?
05What educational practices would make progress faster?

We start with the question: Do broadscale professionals need more multidisciplinary skill?

我们从第一个问题开始：广大专业人士是否需要更多的跨学科技能？

To answer the first question, we must first decide whether more multidisciplinarity will improve professional cognition. And to decide what will cure bad cognition, it will help to know what causes it. One of Bernard Shaw’s characters explained professional defects as follows: “In the last analysis, every profession is a conspiracy against the laity.”

要回答第一个问题，我们必须先判断：更多的跨学科知识能否改善专业人士的认知。而要弄清什么能矫治糟糕的认知，最好先了解其成因。萧伯纳239George Bernard Shaw乔治·萧伯纳（Bernard Shaw）笔下有一位人物曾如此解释专业的缺陷：“说到底，每一种职业都是一场针对外行人的共谋。”

There is a lot of truth in Shaw’s diagnosis, as was early demonstrated when, in the 16th century, the dominant profession, the clergy, burned William Tyndale240William TyndaleWilliam Tyndale (1495–1536) , born in Gloucestershire, England, earned a degree from Oxford and became a priest. He found England hostile to his beliefs and spent time in Germany and Belgium, where he expanded his beliefs and spread the teachings of Martin Luther.威廉·廷代尔（William Tyndale，1495–1536 年）生于英格兰格洛斯特郡，从牛津大学获得学位并成为一名神父。他发现英格兰敌视他的信仰，便在德国和比利时度过了一段时间，在那里他的信仰得以扩展，并传播了马丁·路德（Martin Luther）的教义。 at the stake for translating the Bible into English.

萧伯纳的诊断颇有道理，早期便有明证：十六世纪，占据主导地位的专业人士——教士——因为威廉·廷代尔240William TyndaleWilliam Tyndale (1495–1536) , born in Gloucestershire, England, earned a degree from Oxford and became a priest. He found England hostile to his beliefs and spent time in Germany and Belgium, where he expanded his beliefs and spread the teachings of Martin Luther.威廉·廷代尔（William Tyndale，1495–1536 年）生于英格兰格洛斯特郡，从牛津大学获得学位并成为一名神父。他发现英格兰敌视他的信仰，便在德国和比利时度过了一段时间，在那里他的信仰得以扩展，并传播了马丁·路德（Martin Luther）的教义。（William Tyndale）将《圣经》译成英文，便把他送上了火刑柱。

But Shaw plainly understates the problem in implying that a conscious, self-interested malevolence is the main culprit. More important, there are frequent, terrible effects in professionals from intertwined subconscious mental tendencies, two of which are exceptionally prone to cause trouble: 1) incentive-caused bias, a natural cognitive drift toward the conclusion that what is good for the professional is good for the client and the wider civilization; and 2) man-with-a-hammer tendency, with the name taken from the proverb “To a man with only a hammer, every problem tends to look pretty much like a nail.”

但萧伯纳显然把问题说轻了——他暗示，有意识的、出于私利的恶意才是罪魁祸首。更重要的是，专业人士身上还经常受到交织在一起的潜意识心理倾向的可怕影响，其中有两种格外容易惹麻烦：其一，激励导致的偏见（incentive-caused bias），即一种天然的认知偏向，让人自然而然地得出结论——对专业人士有利的事，对客户和更广大的文明也有利；其二，铁锤人倾向（man-with-a-hammer tendency），其名取自一句谚语：“在只拿着一把锤子的人眼里，所有问题都差不多像一颗钉子。”

One partial cure for man-with-a-hammer tendency is obvious: If a man has a vast set of skills over multiple disciplines, he, by definition, carries multiple tools241Multiple tools多种工具 and therefore will limit bad cognitive effects from man-with-a-hammer tendency. Moreover, when he is multidisciplinary enough to absorb from practical psychology the idea that all his life he must fight bad effects from both the tendencies I mentioned, both within himself and from others, he has taken a constructive step on the road to worldly wisdom.

矫治“铁锤人倾向”的一剂部分解药显而易见：若一个人掌握了许多跨学科的技能，那么按定义他就随身带着多种工具241Multiple tools多种工具，从而能够抑制铁锤人倾向带来的认知恶果。此外，当他拥有足够的跨学科素养，能从实用心理学中领悟到——自己终其一生，都必须与我前面提到的那两种倾向作斗争，无论它们来自自身还是他人——他便在通往普世智慧的路上迈出了建设性的一步。

If A is narrow professional doctrine and B consists of the big, extra-useful concepts from other disciplines, then clearly the professional possessing A plus B will usually be better off than the poor possessor of A alone. How could it be otherwise? And thus, the only rational excuse for not acquiring more B is that it is not practical to do so, given the man’s need for A and the other urgent demands in his life. I will later try to demonstrate that this excuse for unidisciplinarity, at least for our most gifted people, is usually unsound.

如果A是狭隘的专业教条，而B是由其他学科中那些宏大而格外有用的概念构成的，那么显然，同时掌握A加B的专业人士，通常要比只握着A的可怜虫过得更好。事情怎么可能不是这样呢？因此，不去获取更多B的唯一理性借口就是：鉴于一个人需要掌握A，加上生活中其他紧迫的需求，这么做并不现实。稍后我会试图证明，这种固守单一学科的借口——至少对我们中最有天赋的人而言——通常站不住脚。

My second question is so easy to answer that I won’t give it much time. Our education was far too unidisciplinary. Broadscale problems, by definition, cross many academic disciplines. Accordingly, using a unidisciplinary attack on such problems is like playing a bridge hand by counting trumps while ignoring all else. This is bonkers, sort of like the Mad Hatter’s tea party.242Mad Hatter’s tea party疯帽匠的茶会 But nonetheless, too much that is similar remains present in professional practice and, even worse, has long been encouraged in isolated departments of soft science, defined as everything less fundamental than biology.

我的第二个问题太容易回答，我不想多费篇幅。我们的教育太过单一学科化。重大问题按定义会横跨许多学术领域。因此，用单一学科去攻克这类问题，就像打桥牌时只数将牌、对其余一概不顾。这简直荒唐，颇有几分疯帽匠茶会的味道。然而，专业实践中此类做法依然比比皆是，更糟的是，在那些彼此孤立的软科学（soft science，即一切不如生物学基础的学科）院系里，它长期受到推崇。

“重大问题，按定义，会横跨许多学术领域。”

“Broadscale problems, by definition, cross many academic disciplines.”宽泛的问题，按定义就会跨越许多学科。

Even in our youth, some of the best professors were horrified by bad effects from the balkanization of academia into insular, turf-protecting enclaves, wherein notions were maintained by leaps of faith plus exclusion of nonbelievers. Alfred North Whitehead,243Alfred North WhiteheadAlfred North Whitehead (1861–1947) , a British philosopher and mathematician, worked in logic, mathematics, philosophy of science, and metaphysics. Whitehead is known for developing process philosophy, a view holding that fundamental elements of the universe are occasions of experience. In this view, concrete objects are actually successions of these occasions of experience. By grouping occasions of experience, something as complex as a human being can be defined. Whitehead’s views evolved into process theology, a way of understanding God. His best-known mathematics work is Principia Mathematica , cowritten with Bertrand Russell.阿尔弗雷德·诺斯·怀特海（Alfred North Whitehead，1861–1947 年）是英国哲学家和数学家，研究逻辑、数学、科学哲学和形而上学。怀特海以发展过程哲学闻名，该观点认为宇宙的基本元素是“经验的机缘”。依此观点，具体的对象实际上是这些经验机缘的延续。通过对经验机缘加以分组，诸如人类这样复杂的事物也能得到定义。怀特海的观点后来演化为过程神学，一种理解上帝的方式。他最著名的数学著作是与伯特兰·罗素（Bertrand Russell）合著的《数学原理》（Principia Mathematica）。 for one, long ago sounded an alarm in strong language when he spoke of “the fatal unconnectedness of academic disciplines.” And since then, elite educational institutions, agreeing more and more with Whitehead, have steadily fought unconnectedness by bringing in more multidisciplinarity, causing some awesome plaudits to be won in our time by great unconnectedness fighters at the borders of academic disciplines, for instance Harvard’s E. O. Wilson and Caltech’s Linus Pauling. Modern academia now gives more multidisciplinarity than we received and is plainly right to do so.

即便在我们年轻的时候，一些最出色的教授也为学术界割裂成一个个封闭、护短的孤岛而感到震惊——在那里，观念靠信仰的跳跃维系，异见者则被排除在外。阿尔弗雷德·诺斯·怀特海243Alfred North WhiteheadAlfred North Whitehead (1861–1947) , a British philosopher and mathematician, worked in logic, mathematics, philosophy of science, and metaphysics. Whitehead is known for developing process philosophy, a view holding that fundamental elements of the universe are occasions of experience. In this view, concrete objects are actually successions of these occasions of experience. By grouping occasions of experience, something as complex as a human being can be defined. Whitehead’s views evolved into process theology, a way of understanding God. His best-known mathematics work is Principia Mathematica , cowritten with Bertrand Russell.阿尔弗雷德·诺斯·怀特海（Alfred North Whitehead，1861–1947 年）是英国哲学家和数学家，研究逻辑、数学、科学哲学和形而上学。怀特海以发展过程哲学闻名，该观点认为宇宙的基本元素是“经验的机缘”。依此观点，具体的对象实际上是这些经验机缘的延续。通过对经验机缘加以分组，诸如人类这样复杂的事物也能得到定义。怀特海的观点后来演化为过程神学，一种理解上帝的方式。他最著名的数学著作是与伯特兰·罗素（Bertrand Russell）合著的《数学原理》（Principia Mathematica）。（Alfred North Whitehead）便是其中之一，他早在大声疾呼时就曾用强烈的措辞，谈到“学术各学科之间致命的互不连通”。自那以后，精英教育机构越来越认同怀特海，不断地以更多跨学科来对抗割裂，使得我们这个时代里，那些在学科边界上奋勇抗击“互不连通”的斗士赢得了令人赞叹的喝彩，例如哈佛的E. O. 威尔逊（E. O. Wilson）和加州理工学院（Caltech）的莱纳斯·鲍林（Linus Pauling）。现代学术界提供的跨学科程度已超越我们当年所受的，而它这样做显然是对的。

The natural third question then becomes: What is now the goal? What is the essential nature of best-form multidisciplinarity in elite education? This question, too, is easy to answer. All we have to do is examine our most successful narrow-scale education, identify essential elements, and scale up those elements to reach the sensible solution.

于是，自然的第三个问题便浮现出来：如今的目标是什么？精英教育中最理想的跨学科，其本质究竟为何？这个问题同样容易回答。我们只需审视最成功的狭隘型教育，找出其中的关键要素，再把这些要素放大，便能得出合理的解决方案。

To find the best educational narrow-scale model, we have to look not at unthreatened schools of education and the like, too much driven by our two counterproductive psychological tendencies and other bad influences, but instead look where incentives for effective education are strongest and results are most closely measured. This leads us to a logical place: the hugely successful education now mandatory for pilots. Yes, I am suggesting today that mighty Harvard would do better if it thought more about pilot training.

要寻找最理想的狭隘型教育样板，我们不该去看那些没有竞争压力的教育学院之类的地方——它们太受我们那两种适得其反的心理倾向及其他不良影响左右——而该去看教育成效的激励最强、结果考核最严密之处。这把我们引向一个合乎逻辑的去处：如今已成为必修、成效斐然的飞行员训练。是的，我今天想说，伟大的哈佛若能多想想飞行员的训练，情形会更好。

“是的，我今天想说，伟大的哈佛若能多想想飞行员的训练，会做得更好。”

fig 245
—
Pilot training
“Yes, I am suggesting today that mighty Harvard would do better if it thought more about pilot training.”是的，我今天想说的是：若强大的哈佛多想想飞行员的训练，它会做得更好。

In piloting, as in other professions, one great hazard is a bad effect from man-with-a-hammer tendency. We don’t want a pilot, ever, to respond to a hazard as if it was hazard X just because his mind contains only a hazard X model. And so, for that and other reasons, we train a pilot in a strict six-element system:

在飞行中，正如在其他行业里一样，一大隐患便是铁锤人倾向带来的恶果。我们绝不愿意看到：一名飞行员因为脑中只有一个“危险X”的模型，便把任何险情都当做危险X来应对。因此，出于这一点及其他原因，我们用一套严格的六要素体系来训练飞行员：

01His formal education is wide enough to cover practically everything useful in piloting.
02His knowledge of practically everything needed by pilots is not taught just well enough to enable him to pass one test or two; instead, all his knowledge is raised to practice-based fluency, even in handling two or three intertwined hazards at once.
03Like any good algebraist, he is made to think sometimes in a forward fashion and sometimes in reverse, and so he learns when to concentrate mostly on what he wants to happen and also when to concentrate mostly on avoiding what he does not want to happen.
04His training time is allocated among subjects so as to minimize damage from his later malfunctions, and so what is most important in his performance gets the most training coverage and is raised to the highest fluency levels.
05Checklist routines are always mandatory for him.
06Even after original training, he is forced into a special knowledge maintenance routine: regular use of the aircraft simulator to prevent atrophy through long disuse of skills needed to cope with rare and important problems.

The need for this clearly correct six-element system, with its large demands in a narrow-scale field where stakes are high, is rooted in the deep structure of the human mind. Therefore, we must expect that the education we need for broadscale problem-solving will keep all these elements but with awesomely expanded coverage for each element. How could it be otherwise?

这套显然正确的六要素体系，在高风险的专业领域提出了极高要求，其必要性根植于人类心智的深层结构。因此我们必须预期：要解决重大问题所需的教育，必将保留所有这些要素，只是每一要素的覆盖面都要极大地扩展。事情难道还能不是这样吗？

Thus it follows, as the night the day, that in our most elite broadscale education, wherein we are trying to make silk purses out of silk, we need for best results to have multidisciplinary coverage of immense amplitude, with all needed skills raised to an ever-maintained practice-based fluency, including considerable power of synthesis at boundaries between disciplines, with the highest fluency levels being achieved where they are most needed, with forward and reverse thinking techniques being employed in a manner reminding one of inversion in algebra, and with checklist routines being a permanent part of the knowledge system. There can be no other way, no easier way, to broadscale worldly wisdom. Thus the task, when first identified in its immense breadth, seems daunting, verging on impossible.

于是，如同黑夜之后必有白昼，在我们最精英的广义教育中——我们试图用丝绸织出丝囊——若要取得最佳成效，就必须涵盖极广的跨学科内容，将所有必需的技能提升到一种持续保持、基于实践的娴熟程度，包括在学科交界处具备相当的综合能力，在最需要之处达到最高的娴熟水平，采用令人联想到代数中“逆向推导”的正向与逆向思维技巧，并将“检查清单”流程永久纳入知识体系。通往广义普世智慧，再无他途，也再无捷径。因此，当这项任务以其浩瀚的广度初次呈现时，显得令人生畏，几乎不可能完成。

But the task, considered in full context, is far from impossible when we consider three factors:

但若放在完整的语境中，考虑到三个因素，这项任务远非不可能：

First, the concept of “all needed skills” lets us recognize that we don’t have to raise everyone’s skill in celestial mechanics to that of [Pierre-Simon] Laplace246Pierre-Simon LaplacePierre-Simon Laplace (1749–1827) , a French mathematician, astronomer, and philosopher, discovered many key ideas relating to inductive reasoning and probability, celestial movement, and causal determinism. In his great work, A Philosophical Essay on Probabilities , Laplace sets out one of his signature ideas:皮埃尔-西蒙·拉普拉斯（Pierre-Simon Laplace，1749–1827 年）是法国数学家、天文学家和哲学家，发现了许多关于归纳推理与概率、天体运动和因果决定论的关键思想。在他的巨著《概率哲学论》（A Philosophical Essay on Probabilities）中，拉普拉斯阐述了他的一个标志性思想： and also ask everyone to achieve a similar skill level in all other knowledge. Instead, it turns out that the truly big ideas in each discipline, learned only in essence, carry most of the freight. And they are not so numerous, nor are their interactions so complex, that a large and multidisciplinary understanding is impossible for many, given large amounts of talent and time.

首先，“所有必需技能”这一概念让我们认识到，我们不必把每个人的天体力学水平都提升到拉普拉斯247Pierre-Simon Laplace皮埃尔-西蒙·拉普拉斯（Laplace）那般，也不必将其他所有知识都要求到同等水准。事实上，每个学科中那些真正宏大的思想，只需领会其精髓，便能承载大部分的载重。而且它们数量并不算多，彼此的互动也不算太复杂，只要有充分的天赋与时间，许多人都能具备广博的跨学科理解力。

“We may regard the present state of the universe as the effect of its past and the cause of its future. An intellect which at a certain moment would know all forces that set nature in motion, and all positions of all items of which nature is composed, if this intellect were also vast enough to submit these data to analysis, it would embrace in a single formula the movements of the greatest bodies of the universe and those of the tiniest atom; for such an intellect nothing would be uncertain and the future just like the past would be present before its eyes.”

“我们可以把宇宙的现状看作是它过去的结果、未来的原因。假如有某一个智慧，在某一时刻知道驱动自然的一切力量，以及构成自然的一切事物的所有位置；并且，假如这个智慧也足够宏大，能把这些数据提交给分析——那么，它就会把宇宙中最宏大天体的运动和最小原子的运动，都纳入同一个公式之中；对于这样的智慧，没有什么是不确定的，而未来就如同过去，会清晰地呈现在它眼前。”

Second, in elite education, we have available the large amounts of talent and time that we need. After all, we are educating the top 1 percent in aptitude, using teachers who, on average, have more aptitude than the students. And we have roughly 13 long years in which to turn our most promising 12-year-olds into starting professionals.

其次，在精英教育中，我们拥有所需的海量天赋与时间。毕竟，我们培养的是资质位居前百分之一的人，而所用的教师，平均资质又高于学生。我们还有大约十三年漫长的时光，可把最有前途的十二岁少年，打磨成初出茅庐的专业人士。

Third, thinking by inversion and thorough use of checklists is easily learned, in broadscale life as in piloting.

第三，无论是广阔的人生还是飞行，逆向思维与彻底使用检查清单都很容易学会。

Moreover, we can believe in the attainability of broad multidisciplinary skill for the same reason the fellow from Arkansas gave for his belief in baptism:248baptism洗礼 “I’ve seen it done.” We all know of individuals, modern Ben Franklins, who have 1) achieved a massive multidisciplinary synthesis with less time in formal education than is now available to our numerous brilliant young, and 2) thus become better performers in their own disciplines, not worse, despite diversion of learning time to matter outside the normal coverage of their own disciplines.

此外，我们之所以相信广义跨学科技能是可以习得的，理由正与那位阿肯色州（Arkansas）老兄相信洗礼248baptism洗礼相同：“我亲眼见过嘛。”我们都知道一些人——现代的班杰明·富兰克林（Ben Franklin）们——他们（1）所受正规教育的时间，比现在众多聪颖青年所能享有的还要少，却达成了宏大的跨学科综合；（2）因而在自己本行里表现得更出色而非更差，尽管他们把学习时间分去钻研了本学科常规内容之外的事物。

Given the time and talent available and examples of successful masters of multiple disciplines, what is shown by our present failure to minimize bad effects from man-with-a-hammer tendency is only that you can’t win big in multidisciplinarity in soft-science academia if you are so satisfied with the status quo, or so frightened by the difficulties of change, that you don’t try hard enough to win big.

既然时间与天赋俱在，又有众多成功驾驭多学科的大师为榜样，那么我们在抑制铁锤人倾向恶果上的当前失败，只能说明一点：在软科学学术界，如果你安于现状，或被变革的艰难吓倒，以至于不愿全力以赴去赢，你便无法在跨学科上大获全胜。

Which brings us to our fourth question: Judged with reference to an optimized, feasible multidisciplinary goal, how much has elite soft-science education been corrected after we left?

这引出我们的第四个问题：参照一个经过优化、切实可行的跨学科目标来衡量，我们离校之后，精英软科学教育究竟作出了多少修正？

The answer is that many things have been tried as corrections in the direction of better multidisciplinarity. And, after allowing for some counterproductive results, there has been some considerable improvement, net. But much desirable correction is still undone and lies far ahead.

答案是：为了导向更好的跨学科，人们已尝试了许多修正措施。即便扣除一些适得其反的结果，净效果仍是有相当可观的改善。但许多令人期待的修正尚未完成，仍在前方迢迢。

For instance, soft-science academia has increasingly found it helpful when professors from different disciplines collaborate or when a professor has been credentialed in more than one discipline. But a different sort of correction has usually worked best, namely augmentation, or a “take what you wish”249take what you wish取你所愿 practice that encourages any discipline to simply assimilate whatever it chooses from other disciplines. Perhaps it has worked best because it bypassed academic squabbles rooted in the tradition and territoriality that had caused the unidisciplinary folly for which correction was now sought.

例如，软科学学术界日益发现：当不同学科的教授合作，或某位教授拥有多个学科的资格认证时，往往颇有助益。但另一种修正通常效果最佳，那便是增补法，或称“各取所需”（take what you wish）之法——它鼓励任一学科径直吸纳它从其他学科中看中的任何东西。它或许效果最佳，正因为它绕开了那些植根于传统与地盘意识的学术争吵，而正是那种传统与地盘意识，造成了如今亟待修正的单一学科蠢行。

In any event, through increased use of take what you wish, many soft-science disciplines reduced folly from man-with-a-hammer tendency. For instance, led by our classmate Roger Fisher,250Roger FisherRoger Fisher (1922–2012) earned a law degree from Harvard in 1948 and stayed on as a faculty member in the law school. He became director of the Harvard Negotiation Project in 1980. An expert in negotiation and conflict resolution, he coauthored with Bill Ury Getting to Yes, a classic text in win-win negotiation techniques.罗杰·费希尔（Roger Fisher，1922–2012 年）1948 年从哈佛大学获得法律学位，随后留校任法学院教师。他 1980 年出任哈佛谈判项目（Harvard Negotiation Project）主任。作为谈判与冲突解决专家，他与比尔·尤里（Bill Ury）合著了《谈判力》（Getting to Yes），这是双赢谈判技巧的经典文本。 the law schools brought in negotiation, drawing on other disciplines. Over 3 million copies of Roger’s wise and ethical negotiation book have now been sold, and his life’s achievement may well be the best, ever, from our whole class. The law schools also brought in a lot of sound and useful economics, even some good game theory to enlighten antitrust law by better explaining how competition really works.

无论如何，随着“各取所需”的更多采用，许多软科学学科减少了铁锤人倾向带来的蠢行。例如，在我们的同窗罗杰·费舍尔（Roger Fisher）引领下，各法学院引入了借鉴其他学科的谈判学。罗杰那本充满智慧与操守的谈判著作，如今已售出逾三百万册，他一生的成就很可能堪称我们全班有史以来最杰出的。各法学院还引入了大量正确而实用的经济学，甚至一些精妙的博弈论，借以更好地阐明竞争的真实运作，从而启发反垄断法。

Economics, in turn, took in from a biologist the tragedy of the commons model, thus correctly finding a wicked invisible foot in coexistence with Adam Smith’s251Adam SmithAdam Smith (1723–1790) , born in a small village in Scotland, was an exceptional student and entered the University of Glasgow at age 14. He later attended Oxford, returned home to Glasgow, and began an academic career in logic and moral philosophy. His seminal work, The Wealth of Nations, remains the fountainhead of contemporary economic thought. Smith’s explanation of how rational self-interest drives a free market economy greatly influenced thinkers and economists in his own day and in the generations that followed. His work forms the basis of classical economics.亚当·斯密（Adam Smith，1723–1790 年）生于苏格兰一个小村庄，天资过人，14 岁就进入格拉斯哥大学。后来他就读牛津，回到家乡格拉斯哥，开始了逻辑学和道德哲学方向的学术生涯。他的奠基之作《国富论》（The Wealth of Nations）至今仍是当代经济思想的源头。斯密对理性自利如何驱动自由市场经济的解释，极大地影响了同时代及后世的思想家和经济学家。他的著作构成了古典经济学的基础。 angelic invisible hand. These days, there is even some behavioral economics, wisely seeking aid from psychology.

经济学则反过来从一位生物学家那里引入了“公地悲剧”（tragedy of the commons）模型，从而正确地发现了与亚当·斯密251Adam SmithAdam Smith (1723–1790) , born in a small village in Scotland, was an exceptional student and entered the University of Glasgow at age 14. He later attended Oxford, returned home to Glasgow, and began an academic career in logic and moral philosophy. His seminal work, The Wealth of Nations, remains the fountainhead of contemporary economic thought. Smith’s explanation of how rational self-interest drives a free market economy greatly influenced thinkers and economists in his own day and in the generations that followed. His work forms the basis of classical economics.亚当·斯密（Adam Smith，1723–1790 年）生于苏格兰一个小村庄，天资过人，14 岁就进入格拉斯哥大学。后来他就读牛津，回到家乡格拉斯哥，开始了逻辑学和道德哲学方向的学术生涯。他的奠基之作《国富论》（The Wealth of Nations）至今仍是当代经济思想的源头。斯密对理性自利如何驱动自由市场经济的解释，极大地影响了同时代及后世的思想家和经济学家。他的著作构成了古典经济学的基础。（Adam Smith）那天使般的“无形之手”并存的、邪恶的“无形之脚”。如今甚至出现了一些行为经济学，明智地向心理学求援。

“Economics took in from a biologist the tragedy of the commons model, thus correctly finding a wicked invisible foot in coexistence with Adam Smith’s angelic invisible hand.”经济学从一位生物学家那里学来了『公地悲剧』模型，从而正确地发现了一只邪恶的『看不见的脚』，它与亚当·斯密那只天使般的『看不见的手』并存。

However, an extremely permissive practice like take what you wish was not destined to have 100 percent admirable results in soft science. Indeed, in some of its worst outcomes, it helped changes like the assimilation of Freudianism in some literature departments; the importation into many places of extremist political ideologies of the left or right that had, for their possessors, made regaining objectivity almost as unlikely as regaining virginity; and the importation into many law and business schools of hard-form, efficient-market theory by misguided would-be experts in corporate finance, one of whom kept explaining Berkshire Hathaway’s investing success by adding standard deviations of luck until, at six standard deviations, he encountered enough derision to force a change in explanation.

然而，“各取所需”这般极度放任的做法，注定不会在软科学里结出百分之百可喜的果实。确实，在它最糟糕的一些后果中，它助长了诸般变化，例如：某些文学系吸纳了弗洛伊德主义252Freudianism弗洛伊德主义；许多地方引进了极左或极右的极端政治意识形态，对其持有者而言，重获客观几乎如同重获童贞般不可能；以及（3）许多法学院与商学院被误入歧途的公司理财“准专家”们引入了生硬的有效市场理论（efficient market theory），其中一人为了解释伯克希尔·哈撒韦（Berkshire Hathaway）的投资成功，不断往上叠加运气的“标准差”，直到叠加到六个标准差，招致的嘲笑才足以迫使他改口。

Moreover, even when it avoided such lunacies, take what you wish had some serious defects. For instance, takings from more fundamental disciplines were often done without attribution, sometimes under new names, with little attention given to rank in a fundamentalness order for absorbed concepts. Such practices 1) act like a lousy filing system that must impair the successful use and synthesis of absorbed knowledge, and 2) do not maximize in soft science the equivalent of Linus Pauling’s systematic mining of physics to improve chemistry. There must be a better way.

此外，即便“各取所需”避开了这类癫狂，它仍有些严重的缺陷。例如，从更基础的学科中取材时，往往不加注明，有时还另起新名，几乎不理会所吸纳概念在基础性序列中的位次。此类做法（1）宛如一套糟糕的归档系统，必然妨碍对所吸收知识的成功运用与综合；（2）也未能在软科学中最大化出堪比莱纳斯·鲍林系统挖掘物理学以改进化258evolution进化学的成效。一定有更好的路子。

This brings us, finally, to our last question: In elite soft science, what practices would hasten our progress toward optimized disciplinarity? Here, again, there are some easy answers:

最后，这把我们引向最后一个问题：在精英软科学中，哪些做法能加速我们逼近最优的学科格局？这里同样有些现成的答案：

First, many more courses should be mandatory, not optional. And this, in turn, requires that the people who decide what is mandatory must possess large, multidisciplinary knowledge maintained in fluency. This conclusion is as obvious in the training of the would-be broadscale problem-solver as it is in the training of the would-be pilot. For instance, both psychology mastery and accounting mastery should be required as outcomes in legal education. Yet in many elite places, even today, there are no such requirements. Often, such is the narrowness of mind of the program designers that they neither see what is needed and missing nor are able to fix deficiencies.

第一，应有更多课程成为必修，而非选修。而这反过来要求：决定何为必修的人，自己必须掌握广博、且保持娴熟的跨学科知识。这一结论，无论对未来的广义问题解决者还是未来的飞行员之培养，都同样显明。例如，心理学精通与会计精通，都应在法学教育中作为必达的目标。然而即便今日，许多精英学府仍无此类要求。制定培养方案者心胸之狭隘，往往到了既看不出所需何物、缺失何在，又无力弥补缺陷的地步。

“应有更多课程成为必修，而非选修。而这反过来要求：决定何为必修的人，自己必须掌握广博、且保持娴熟的跨学科知识。”

“Many more courses should be mandatory, not optional. And this, in turn, requires that the people who decide what is mandatory must possess large, multidisciplinary knowledge maintained in fluency.”更多的课程应当必修，而非选修。而这反过来要求：决定何为必修的人，自身必须掌握广博、多学科且运用纯熟的知识。

Second, there should be much more problem-solving practice that crosses several disciplines, including practice that mimics the function of the aircraft simulator in preventing loss of skills through disuse.

第二，应有远为更多的、横跨若干学科的解决问题练习，包括那些仿效飞行模拟器功能、防止技能因荒废而退化的练习。

Let me give an example, roughly remembered, of this sort of teaching by a very wise but untypical Harvard Business School professor many decades ago. This professor gave a test involving two unworldly old ladies who had just inherited a New England shoe factory254shoe factory鞋厂 making branded shoes and beset with serious business problems described in great detail. The professor then gave the students ample time to answer with written advice to the old ladies. In response to the answers, the professor gave every student an undesirable grade except for one student who was graded at the top by a wide margin.

让我举一个大致记得的例子，说说几十年前哈佛商学院一位极有智慧却不循常规的教授的这种教法。这位教授出了一道考题：两位不谙世故的老太太刚继承了一家新英格兰的鞋厂254shoe factory鞋厂，该厂生产自有品牌的鞋，正深陷严重的经营困境，详情被描述得纤毫毕现。教授给了学生充裕的时间，让他们写下给两位老太太的建议。阅完答卷，教授给每个学生都打了不及格，唯独一名学生以极大优势名列榜首。

What was the winning answer? It was very short and roughly as follows: “This business field and this particular business, in its particular location, present crucial problems that are so difficult that unworldly old ladies cannot wisely try to solve them through hired help. Given the difficulties and unavoidable agency costs, the old ladies should promptly sell the shoe factory, probably to the competitor who would enjoy the greatest marginal utility advantage.”

那个夺魁的答案是什么？它非常简短，大意如下：“这个行业，以及这家身处特定地点的特定企业，所呈现的关键难题如此棘手，以至于不谙世故的老太太根本无法靠雇人明智地解决。鉴于难题与不可避免的代理成本（agency costs），老太太们应当尽快卖掉鞋厂，大抵卖给那位能享有最大边际效用（marginal utility）优势的竞争对手。”

Thus, the winning answer relied not on what the students had most recently been taught in business school but instead on more fundamental concepts, like agency costs and marginal utility, lifted from undergraduate psychology and economics. Ah, my fellow members of the Harvard Law Class of 1948—if only we had been much more often tested like that, just think of what more we might have accomplished!

由此可见，那个夺魁的答案所倚仗的，并非学生在商学院刚学过的内容，而是更基本的概念，如代理成本与边际效用，取自本科的心理学与经济学。啊，我哈佛法学院1948届的同学们——倘若当年我们也能更多接受这样的考验，试想我们本可成就何等更多的事业！

Incidentally, many elite private schools now wisely use such multidisciplinary methods in seventh grade science, while at the same time many graduate schools have not yet seen the same light. This is one more sad example of Whitehead’s fatal unconnectedness in education.

顺带一提，如今许多精英私立学校已在七年级科学课中明智地采用此类跨学科方法，而与此同时，许多研究生院却尚未领悟同样的道理。这又是怀特海所言“教育中致命的互不连通”的又一可悲例证。

“如今许多精英私立学校已在七年级科学课中明智地采用此类跨学科方法，而与此同时，许多研究生院却尚未领悟同样的道理。”

“Many elite private schools now wisely use such multidisciplinary methods in seventh grade science, while at the same time many graduate schools have not yet seen the same light.”如今许多精英私立学校已明智地在七年级科学课中运用这种多学科方法，而与此同时，许多研究生院却尚未见到同样的光亮。

Third, most soft-science professional schools should increase use of the best business periodicals, like the Wall Street Journal, Forbes, Fortune, etc. Such periodicals are now quite good and perform the function of the aircraft simulator if used to prompt practice in relating events to multidisciplinary causes, often intertwined. And sometimes the periodicals even introduce new models for causes instead of merely refreshing old knowledge. Also, it is not just slightly sound to have the student practice in school what he must practice lifelong after formal education is over if he is going to maximize his good judgment. I know no person in business, respected for verified good judgment, whose wisdom maintenance system does not include use of such periodicals. Why should academia be different?

第三，大多数软科学专业学院应当更多地使用一流的财经期刊，如《华尔街日报》（The Wall Street Journal）、《福布斯》（Forbes）、《财富》（Fortune）等。这类刊物如今已相当出色，若用来引导学生练习将事件关联到往往相互交织的跨学科成因上，便能发挥飞行模拟器的功能。有时这些刊物甚至会引入新的成因模型，而不只是重温旧知。再者，若想让学生最大化其良好判断力，让他在校期间就操练那套正规教育结束后须终其一生操练的功夫，绝非仅有一点点道理。在我所识的商界人士中，但凡以经证实的良好判断力受人敬重者，其智慧维护系统无不包括对这些刊物的使用。学术界凭什么该是例外？

Fourth, in filling scarce academic vacancies, professors of superstrong, passionate political ideology, whether on the left or right, should usually be avoided. So also for students. Best-form multidisciplinarity requires an objectivity such passionate people have lost, and a difficult synthesis is not likely to be achieved by minds in ideological fetters. In our day, some Harvard Law professors could and did point to a wonderful example of just such ideology-based folly. This, of course, was the law school at Yale, which was then viewed by many at Harvard as trying to improve legal education by importing a particular political ideology as a dominant factor.

第四，在填补稀缺的学术空缺时，通常应当避开那些抱有极度强烈、狂热的政治意识形态的教授，无论左翼还是右翼。对学生亦应如此。最理想的跨学科需要一种客观，而此类狂热者早已丧失；被意识形态锁链捆住的心智，也绝难达成艰难的综合。在我们那个年代，哈佛法学院一些教授能够、也确实指出了一个恰是此类意识形态蠢行的绝佳范例。这当然便是耶鲁（Yale）的法学院——当时许多哈佛人视之为：试图通过引入某种特定的政治意识形态作为主导因素，来改善法学教育。

Fifth, soft science should more intensely imitate the fundamental organizing ethos of hard science, defined as the fundamental four-discipline combination of math, physics, chemistry, and engineering. This ethos deserves more imitation. After all, hard science has, by a wide margin, the best record for both 1) avoiding unidisciplinary folly and 2) making user-friendly a big patch of multidisciplinary domain, with frequent, good results like those of physicist Richard Feynman255Richard P. He worked on the Manhattan Project and was instrumental in the development of the atomic bomb. He held faculty posts at Cornell University until 1951 and then settled at Caltech. Feynman’s major contribution to physics was in quantum electrodynamics, the study of the interactions of electromagnetic radiation with atoms and more fundamental particles. He shared the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1965. Late in life, Feynman was named to the commission that investigated the Challenger Space Shuttle accident. He demonstrated the effect of cold temperatures on rubber O-rings and showed how the resulting shrinkage allowed hot gasses to escape, causing the explosion.理查德·P·费曼（Richard P. Feynman，1918–1988 年）生于纽约远洛克威。他从麻省理工学院获得物理学本科学位，随后赴普林斯顿攻读博士。他参与了曼哈顿计划，对原子弹的研制起了重要作用。他先后在康奈尔大学任教至 1951 年，之后定居加州理工学院。费曼对物理学的主要贡献在量子电动力学——研究电磁辐射与原子及更基本粒子的相互作用。1965 年，他分享了诺贝尔物理学奖。晚年，费曼被任命为调查挑战者号航天飞机事故的委员会成员。他演示了低温对橡胶 O 型圈的影响，并说明由此产生的收缩如何让高温气体逸出，从而引发爆炸。 when he so quickly found in cold O-rings the cause of our greatest space shuttle disaster.

第五，软科学应当更着力地模仿硬科学（hard science，即数学、物理学、化学与工程学这四大基础学科的结合）的根本性治学精神。这种精神值得更多地效法。毕竟，硬科学在两方面遥遥领先：其一，避免单一学科的蠢行；其二，让一大片跨学科领域变得平易可用，并频结善果，例如物理学家理查德·费曼255Richard P. FeynmanRichard P. He worked on the Manhattan Project and was instrumental in the development of the atomic bomb. He held faculty posts at Cornell University until 1951 and then settled at Caltech. Feynman’s major contribution to physics was in quantum electrodynamics, the study of the interactions of electromagnetic radiation with atoms and more fundamental particles. He shared the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1965. Late in life, Feynman was named to the commission that investigated the Challenger Space Shuttle accident. He demonstrated the effect of cold temperatures on rubber O-rings and showed how the resulting shrinkage allowed hot gasses to escape, causing the explosion.理查德·P·费曼（Richard P. Feynman，1918–1988 年）生于纽约远洛克威。他从麻省理工学院获得物理学本科学位，随后赴普林斯顿攻读博士。他参与了曼哈顿计划，对原子弹的研制起了重要作用。他先后在康奈尔大学任教至 1951 年，之后定居加州理工学院。费曼对物理学的主要贡献在量子电动力学——研究电磁辐射与原子及更基本粒子的相互作用。1965 年，他分享了诺贝尔物理学奖。晚年，费曼被任命为调查挑战者号航天飞机事故的委员会成员。他演示了低温对橡胶 O 型圈的影响，并说明由此产生的收缩如何让高温气体逸出，从而引发爆炸。（Richard Feynman）就曾如此迅速地，从冰冷的O形环中找出了那场最惨重航天飞机灾难的肇因。

Previous extensions of the ethos into softer fare have worked well. For instance, biology, starting 150 years ago with a descriptive mess not much related to deep theory, has gradually absorbed the fundamental organizing ethos with marvelous results, as new generations have come to use better thinking methods containing models that answer the question “Why?” And there is no clear reason why the ethos of hard science can’t also help in disciplines far less fundamental than biology.

此前将这种精神延展到较软的领域，已颇见成效。例如，生物学在一百五十年前还只是一团与深层理论无甚关联的描述性乱麻，却逐渐吸纳了这种根本性治学精神，结果蔚为壮观——新一代学者开始运用更好的思维方法，其模型能回答“为什么”的问题。而硬科学的精神既然帮得上生物学，便没有清晰理由说它不能惠及那些远不如生物学基础的学科。

Here, as I interpret it, is this fundamental organizing ethos I am talking about:

依我所见，我所说的这种根本性治学精神如下：

01You must both rank and use disciplines in order of fundamentalness.
02You must, like it or not, master to tested fluency and routinely use the truly essential parts of all four constituents of the fundamental four-discipline combination, with particularly intense attention given to disciplines more fundamental than your own.
03You may never practice either cross-disciplinary absorption without attribution or departure from a principle of economy that forbids explaining in any other way anything readily explainable from more fundamental material in your own or any other discipline.
04But when the step 3 approach doesn’t produce much new and useful insight, you should hypothesize and test to establishment new principles, ordinarily by using methods similar to those that created successful old principles. But you may not use any new principle inconsistent with an old one unless you can now prove that the old principle is not true.

You will note that, compared with much current practice in soft science, the fundamental organizing ethos of hard science is more severe. This reminds one of pilot training, and this outcome is not a coincidence. Reality is talking to anyone who will listen. Like pilot training, the ethos of hard science does not say “Take what you wish” but “Learn it all to fluency, like it or not.” And rational organization of multidisciplinary knowledge is forced by making mandatory 1) full attribution for cross-disciplinary takings and 2) mandatory preference for the most fundamental explanation.

你会注意到，与软科学当前的许多做法相比，硬科学的根本性治学精神要严苛得多。这令人想起飞行员的训练，而这一结果并非巧合。现实在对任何愿意聆听的人说话。与飞行训练一样，硬科学的治学精神不说“各取所需”，而是“不论喜恶，全部学到娴熟”。而跨学科知识的理性组织，是通过两条强制规定来实现的：（1）对跨学科的取材必须完全注明出处；（2）必须优先采用最基础的解释。

This simple idea may appear too obvious to be useful, but there is an old two-part rule that often works wonders in business, science, and elsewhere: 1) Take a simple, basic idea and 2) take it very seriously. And as some evidence for the value of taking very seriously the fundamental organizing ethos, I offer the example of my own life.

这个朴素的想法看似太过显然而派不上用场，但商界、科学界及其他领域里常有一条古老的两步法则能创造奇迹：其一，找到一个简单而基本的道理；其二，极认真地对待它。至于“极认真对待根本性治学精神”的价值，我愿以自己的一生作为佐证。

“商界、科学界及其他领域里常有一条古老的两步法则能创造奇迹：其一，找到一个简单而基本的道理；其二，极认真地对待它。”

fig 256
—
The example of my own life
“There is an old two-part rule that often works wonders in business, science, and elsewhere: 1) Take a simple, basic idea and 2) take it very seriously.”有句古老的两段式法则，常在商业、科学及其他领域创造奇迹：一、取一个简单的基本观念；二、极其认真地对待它。

I came to Harvard Law School very poorly educated, with desultory work habits and no college degree. I was admitted over the objection of Warren Abner Seavey through the intervention of family friend Roscoe Pound.257Roscoe Pound罗斯科·庞德 I had taken one silly course in biology in high school, briefly learning, mostly by rote, an obviously incomplete theory of evolution,258evolution进化 portions of the anatomy of the paramecium259paramecium草履虫 and frog,260frog青蛙 plus a ridiculous concept of “protoplasm” that has since disappeared.

我进入哈佛法学院时受教育极少，学习习惯散漫，也没有大学学位。我是在沃伦·阿博纳·希维（Warren Abner Seavey）反对的情况下，经由世交罗斯科·庞德257Roscoe Pound罗斯科·庞德（Roscoe Pound）的斡旋才被录取的。高中时我修过一门荒唐的生物课，大多靠死记硬背，粗浅学了个明显不完整的进化论，草履虫259paramecium草履虫与青蛙260frog青蛙解剖的若干片段，外加一个后来已销声匿迹的荒唐概念——“原生质”。

To this day, I have never taken any course, anywhere, in chemistry, economics, psychology, or business. But I early took elementary physics and math and paid enough attention to somehow assimilate the fundamental organizing ethos of hard science, which I thereafter pushed further and further into softer and softer fare as my organizing guide and filing system in a search for whatever multidisciplinary worldly wisdom it would be easy to get.

时至今日，我在任何地方都从未修过化学、经济学、心理学或商学的课程。但我早年学过基础物理与数学，并足够用心地、不知不觉间吸纳了硬科学的根本性治学精神；此后，我把它当作组织指南与归档系统，越来越深地推入越来越软的领域，去搜寻那些容易到手的跨学科普世智慧。

Thus, my life became a sort of accidental educational experiment with respect to the feasibility and utility of a very gross academic extension of the fundamental organizing ethos by a man who also learned well what his own discipline had to teach.

于是，我的人生无意间成了一场教育实验，关乎这样一种可行性及效用：一个也学通了本门学科精髓的人，将根本性治学精神极大限度地延展到学术疆域之外。

What I found, in my extended attempts to complete by informal means my stunted education, was that, plugging along with only ordinary will but with the fundamental organizing ethos as my guide, my ability to serve everything I loved was enhanced far beyond my deserts. Large gains came in places that seemed unlikely as I started out, sometimes making me like the only one without a blindfold in a high-stakes game of pin the tail on the donkey. For instance, I was productively led into psychology, where I had no plans to go, creating large advantages that deserve a story on another day.

在我以非正式手段补足那残缺教育的漫长尝试中，我发现：仅凭寻常的意志，却以根本性治学精神为指引，我服务所爱一切的能力，竟得到了远超我应得的提升。巨大的收获来自起步时看似绝无可能之处，有时令我宛如那场高风险“蒙眼钉驴尾”游戏中唯一未被蒙住眼睛的人。例如，我被卓有成效地引入了心理学——那本非我计划前往之地——由此生出的巨大优势，值得改日另述。

Today, I have no more story. I have finished my talk by answering my own questions as best I could in a brief time. What is most interesting to me in my answers is that, while everything I have said is non-original and has long been obvious to the point of banality to many sound and well-educated minds, all the evils I decry remain grossly over-present in the best of our soft-science educational domains, wherein virtually every professor has a too-unidisciplinary habit of mind, even while a better model exists just across the aisle in his own university.

今天，我没有更多故事可讲了。我以在简短时间内尽力自问自答，结束了这次演说。在我的回答中，最令我感兴趣的莫过于：尽管我所说的一切皆非原创，对许多理性而受过良好教育的心智而言，早已平庸到近乎老生常谈，但我所痛斥的那些弊病，在我们最顶尖的软科学教育领域中却依然严重过剩——在那里，几乎每位教授都养成了太过单一学科的思维习惯，即便在他自己大学里，更好的榜样就隔着一条过道。

To me, this ridiculous outcome implies that the soft-science departments tolerate perverse incentives. Wrong incentives are a major cause because, as Dr. Samuel Johnson261Samuel JohnsonSamuel Johnson (1709–1784) , English author and the leading literary scholar and critic of his time, was celebrated for his brilliant and witty conversation. Johnson’s first work of lasting importance, and the one that permanently established his reputation, was his Dictionary of the English Language (1755).塞缪尔·约翰逊（Samuel Johnson，1709–1784 年），英国作家，是他那个时代最杰出的文学学者和批评家，以机敏睿智的谈吐闻名。约翰逊第一部具有持久重要性、也永久奠定其声誉的著作，是他的《英语词典》（Dictionary of the English Language，1755）。 so wisely observed, truth is hard to assimilate in any mind when opposed by interest. And if institutional incentives cause the problem, then a remedy is feasible, because incentives can be changed.

“当真理与利益相悖时，任何心智都难以吸纳它。”

“Truth is hard to assimilate in any mind when opposed by interest.”当真相与利益相关相对立时，任何心智都难以吸收它。

I have tried to demonstrate today, and indeed by the example of my life, that it is neither inevitable nor advantageous for soft-science educational domains to tolerate as much unidisciplinary wrongheadedness as they now do. Please remember the word Dr. Johnson used to describe maintenance of academic ignorance that is removable through diligence: To Dr. Johnson, such conduct was “treachery.”

我今天力图证明——事实上也以我的人生为证——软科学教育领域容忍眼下这般多的单一学科谬见，既非不可避免，也毫无益处。请记住约翰逊261Samuel JohnsonSamuel Johnson (1709–1784) , English author and the leading literary scholar and critic of his time, was celebrated for his brilliant and witty conversation. Johnson’s first work of lasting importance, and the one that permanently established his reputation, was his Dictionary of the English Language (1755).塞缪尔·约翰逊（Samuel Johnson，1709–1784 年），英国作家，是他那个时代最杰出的文学学者和批评家，以机敏睿智的谈吐闻名。约翰逊第一部具有持久重要性、也永久奠定其声誉的著作，是他的《英语词典》（Dictionary of the English Language，1755）。博士用来描述“本可经勤勉消除的学识无知”的那个词：在约翰逊博士眼中，这种行为便是“背叛”（treachery）。

And if duty will not move improvement, advantage is also available. There will be immense worldly rewards, for law schools and other academic domains as for Charlie Munger, in a more multidisciplinary approach to many problems, common or uncommon. And more fun, as well as more accomplishment. The happier mental realm I recommend is one from which no one willingly returns. A return would be like cutting off one’s hands.

倘若责任不足以推动改进，利益也照样垂手可得。对法学院、对其他学术领域，正如对查理·芒格（Charlie Munger）一样，以更跨学科的路径去应对诸多或寻常或罕见的问题，将带来巨大的世俗回报。还会有更多乐趣，以及更多成就。我所推荐的那种更愉悦的心智境界，是无人愿意从中返回的；返回，无异于砍掉自己的双手。

“我所推荐的那种更愉悦的心智境界，是无人愿意从中返回的；返回，无异于砍掉自己的双手。”

“The happier mental realm I recommend is one from which no one willingly returns. A return would be like cutting off one’s hands.”我所推荐的那个更快乐的心智之境，无人愿意主动离开。离开它，无异于切断自己的双手。
